The documentation covers the three parts of a workflow: the task and its labels, the learner that predicts a penalty, and the measures and plots that check it. This page lists the main objects, shows how the package is organised and explains the idea behind penalty learning. The sidebar links to each part.

## Main objects and functions

Every learner has the same interface, so code written for one runs with the others.

| Object or function | What it does |
|--------------------|--------------|
| `TaskCpt$new()` | Stores one row per sequence: the signal and its labelled regions. |
| `lrn("changepoint.intregrcv")`, `lrn("changepoint.xgboost.aft")`, `lrn("changepoint.mmit")`, `lrn("changepoint.mmif")` | Creates a learner, which predicts a penalty for each sequence. |
| `$train(task)` | Fits the learner to the labelled sequences. |
| `$predict(task)` | Returns a `PredictionCpt` with the predicted `log(lambda)` of each sequence. |
| `msr("changepoint.label_error")`, `msr("changepoint.label_accuracy")`, `msr("changepoint.auc")` | Creates a measure. |
| `$score(measures, task = task)` | Scores a prediction against the labels. |
| `autoplot(task)` | Plots the sequences with their labelled regions. |
| `autoplot(prediction, task = task)` | Adds the changes or peaks selected by the predicted penalties. |
| `autoplot(prediction, task = task, type = "roc")` | Plots the ROC curve. |
| `resample()`, `benchmark()`, `auto_tuner()` | Resampling, benchmarking and tuning from mlr3 and mlr3tuning, unchanged. |

## How the package is organised

For one sequence, a solver computes the best model of each complexity $k$ up to a cap, `Kmax`. The complexity is the number of segments for changepoint labels and the number of peaks for peak labels. A penalty $\lambda > 0$ selects one of these models:

$$k^*(\lambda) = \arg\min_{k} \; \text{loss}(k) + \lambda k.$$

The labels of a sequence are right for some models and wrong for others, so they define an interval of $\log \lambda$ values with the fewest label errors: the target interval. A learner computes features $x_i$ of each sequence $i$ and fits a function $f(x_i)$ that predicts $\log \lambda_i$ inside its target interval. On a new sequence, the predicted penalty selects the model.

The package follows the same split.
